blocks.heading: Social cost in this syllabus
blocks.text: Social costs are the costs paid by the rest of society, rather than the business, as a result of a business decision; they are also known as external costs in this syllabus. Identify the affected outsiders and the consequence they bear. The firm’s own material or wage bill is a private cost, not the same category. Some texts use social cost more broadly, so use the stated syllabus meaning consistently in these resources. A cost need not appear on the business’s accounts to matter to the community.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Eha Works pays its material bill but creates noise that disturbs neighbouring households. The material bill is its private cost. Neighbours’ disturbance is the external or social cost in the syllabus sense.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Descriptive social effects and regulation
blocks.text:
Fictional Omi Materials proposes a workshop with shared access improvements but noise affecting neighbours. An effective enclosure and daytime schedule can reduce the disturbance at a manageable cost. It compares monitored conditions with refusal.

Evaluate Omi’s controlled-operation option against refusal under the original facts. Give a concise descriptive plan. [12]

Identify parties: business private return, other users’ access benefit and neighbours’ noise cost. Compare effective enclosure/daytime operation with refusal. Control preserves benefits but needs cost, maintenance and monitoring; refusal avoids this harm but loses the project benefits. Judgement: conditional operation while protection is effective. Do not count arguments as if their number establishes the balance or assume every effect has a precise money figure.
